note: Manual quality findings (D-238's MF-1 and MF-2) in a register of their own: the findings register stays byte for byte the one D-223, D-225, D-231 and D-232 pinned. A pipeline run reads both when its manifest names reviewRegister. An open finding keeps an outfit from being ready, whatever the automatic checks say. D-239 adds F-015 … F-019: the tops whose open hip corners leave bites below COMBO-6's threshold.

findings.where: the hem over a shoe, y ≈ 1374–1382 (both legs)
findings.what: D-238 MF-1: skin-coloured pieces along the hem — (a) the hem contour antialiased with the picture's SHADED skin, left opaque in the layer (orange dots over a black boot; the mechanism of F-001), corrected in method d239 by unmixing against the picture's own skin; (b) C's ankle seen 6–7 rows between the hem and a low shoe's front collar (an orange wedge over the white sneakers) — a real gap, no extraction fault, caught in d239 by the outfit check COMBO-5. Open until the owner has reviewed the d239 result.
findings.decision: D-238 found, D-239 corrected (a) and checks (b)

findings.where: both hips just below the tank, y ≈ 780–797
findings.what: D-238 MF-2: a notch in the outline at the hips. Not the trousers' layer: their outline there lies over C's base-top corner, another category's base, which an item never takes; the tank leaves that corner open (SC-W2, F-011/F-012's kind), so nothing covers it and background shows. The picture of the top lacks the fabric — marked, never filled: caught in d239 by the outfit check COMBO-6. Open until the owner has reviewed.

findings.where: both hips, the rows of C's base-top corner just above its base shorts (y ≈ 770–815)
findings.what: the tank (pilot) leaves C's base-top hip corners open (SC-W2): no bottom may take another category's base, so every outfit with it shows background at the hips. COMBO-6 (d239) rejects the deep notches (≥ 3 rows 3 px deep with a 3 px step in the outline); smaller bites of 1–3 px stay visible at full size in outfits the checks pass. The picture lacks the fabric — marked, never filled. A top that covers its corners (N1, V1) leaves none.
